searchText: What if we simply call it `ExecutionLayerRequest` as a short name of `ExecutionLayerAuthorizedBeaconChainRequest` (the latter reminds me of Java) What is the argument defending the removal of useful information from a variable name in favor of it being shorter? What significant value is provided by having a "short" name that is worth losing useful information in the name? I think that if a name contains key words that are enough for most readers or listeners to understand the thing then it can stay short, no need to make it longer as ppl will likely pronounce only a subset of those key words One more thing is that if you make the variable name generic, it's easier to add things to the variable without having to come up with new, longer names. For example, if we want to include a EL operation `Xyz` in the F-fork, we can keep the name `ExecutionLayerRequest` , possibly adding a `V2` suffix. If we name it `ExecutionLayerExitAndWithdrawal` now, then it will have to be `ExecutionLayerExitAndWithdrawalAndXyz`... You see the point. Generalization is a double edged-sword though, because you can put basically anything under a very generally-named object and make it monstrous, and contain many unrelated responsibilities. So one point of discussion is do we foresee if there will be more other kinds of requests from EL in the future that it’s useful to have a generic name? It can be withdrawal creds rotation, consolidations, etc. But i would not commit to anything rn That the people that typically defend the useful information in the variable name are not the ones that are coding all day 😂 I personally find that most variables that take more than a couple of characters hurt reading the code, specially if they are used in a single local function: it's much simpler to have the declaration close to the usage and it be just one or two characters I feel the opposite about getters that can be accessed from anywhere. I favor: ``` x = here_is_my_descriptive_getter() ... use_fn(x) ``` yeah i'm not proposing we lose information, but if two names are roughly equal in info we should obviously favor the shorter I agree with this! Basically we had this terminology for 7002 before: "Exit" and now we are moving to "WithdrawalRequest". I don't think either are quite accurate because with partial withdrawals, this request can either be i) full exit of validator entity ii) partial withdrawal of validator funds I am kinda leaning back towards "Exit" as the terminology and referring to less than full exits as partial exits (since you are kinda reducing the stake of the validator, "exiting" some it's weight) i want to ask a staking question here - what kind of staking data does the beacon node hold? and whether we can use that data to do some useful analysis?
